mentions.name: tlsproxy
mentions.description: A high-performance TLS proxy and TLS terminator that handles 3000 TLS handshakes per second, positioned as a replacement for stunnel. It matches nginx and HAProxy's speed (bottlenecked only by OpenSSL crypto) while offering a tiny fraction of the attack surface and a 10-15kb memory footprint per worker process. Still in development, with planned features including privilege dropping, in-place config reloads, log burst suppression, multiple listen sockets (enabling free load balancing with the Linux kernel), and detailed TLS configurability.
mentions.problem: stunnel crashes at under 100 TLS handshakes per second, leaving a gap for a fast, lightweight TLS termination tool.
mentions.source_excerpt: I’ve been working on a TLS proxy/TLS terminator that can handle 3000 TLS handshakes per second (basically an stunnel replacement, but stunnel crashes at under 100 handshakes per second) as a pet project, but I’ve realized that with some polishing this can be really useful.
